problem:
The population $P(t)$ of customers signed up for a grocery store’s rewards program follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.35P-0.0007{P}^{2},
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in months. If there were $120$ customers signed up initially, how many customers were signed up after $7$ months? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

After $7$ months, approximately
{{field-1}} customers were signed up.

feedback.problem:
The growth rate of the number of trees in a reforestation area, $P(t),$ is jointly proportional to the number of trees at time $t,$ measured in years, and the difference between the area’s carrying capacity and the number of trees.

Given that the constant of proportionality is $\frac{1}{3000}$ and the carrying capacity is $1500,$ find an expression for the number of trees after $t$ years, given that there were $300$ trees in the area initially.

| $P(t)\,=\,\,$ | $1500$ |
| --- | --- |
| $1\,+\,$ {{field-1}} |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the number of trees grows at a rate that is *jointly* proportional to the number of trees at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the number of trees, the number of trees follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=\frac{1}{3000},$ and the carrying capacity is $a=1500.$ Therefore, the growth is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=\frac{1}{3000}\,P(1500-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{1500}{1+C{e}^{-(1500\cdot \frac{1}{3000})t}}=\frac{1500}{1+C{e}^{-t/2}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=300$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1500}{1+C{e}^{-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 0}} & =300 \\ 1+C & =\frac{1500}{300} \\ C & =5-1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{1500}{1+4{e}^{-t/2}}.
$$
